title: Refunds of Set-Aside Disbursements and Reversed Fee Draws
content:
This rule of Set-Aside Accounts covers money that comes back after a set-aside paid it out: a refund from a taxing authority or insurer of a disbursement the set-aside made (a duplicate or overpaid tax installment, or the unearned premium of a cancelled policy), and the reversal of an erroneous servicing fee on the loan.

## Clauses

1. When such a refund is made, or an erroneous servicing fee is reversed, the refunded amount is credited back to the set-aside as the plan's refund-credit setting directs, referencing the original disbursement or fee draw, and is reversed from the HECM loan balance.
2. A refund is credited to the set-aside only while the set-aside status is active, as the set-aside record shows.
3. A refund that arrives after the set-aside is depleted, cancelled or closed is not credited to the set-aside; it is applied, as the plan's setting for refunds after closing directs, as a reduction of the loan balance.
4. A refund credit never exceeds the original disbursement, and each original disbursement or fee draw is refunded at most once.

## Retired clause

The words of clause 1 "the refunded amount is credited back to the set-aside" as the plan's refund-credit setting directs are **no longer in force** for three kinds of money paid back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, each of which is now credited at its kept amount under the current basis rather than at the whole refunded amount:

- a property tax refund that a taxing authority mailed to the borrower and that the borrower pays back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve;
- a hazard insurance premium that an insurer returned to the borrower or the borrower's estate after a reserve-paid term was withdrawn, and that is paid back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve;
- a flood insurance premium that an insurer returned to the borrower or the borrower's estate after a reserve-paid term was withdrawn, and that is paid back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve.

Every other refund continues to be credited under clause 1 as written. Clauses 2 to 4 remain in force for every refund.

## Hypothetical cases

| Situation | Set-aside status | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| County returns 400.00 of a duplicate tax installment paid directly to it from a LESA | Active | Credited to the set-aside, referencing the original installment payment |
| Erroneous servicing fee of 35.00 reversed on the loan | Active | Credited back to the Servicing Fee Set-Aside, referencing the fee draw |
| Insurer returns 300.00 of unearned premium | Closed | Not credited to the set-aside; applied as a reduction of the loan balance |
| A second refund against the same original payment | Any | Not credited; each original is refunded at most once |

superseded_clauses: the refunded amount is credited back to the set-aside per refund_credit_target
